{{Short description|Russian mathematician}}{{BLP}}

'''Dmitri Yurievich Burago''' ({{Langx|ru|Дмитрий Юрьевич Бураго}}, born May 17, 1964) is a leading Russian-American [[mathematician]], specializing in [[Differential geometry|differential]], [[Riemannian geometry|Riemannian]], [[Finsler]] geometry, [[geometric analysis]], [[dynamical systems]], and applications to [[mathematical physics]]. 

He is the son of the celebrated [[Geometer]] and Russian [[mathematician]] [[Yuri Burago]], with whom he also published well known book on metric geometry. Burago studied at [[45th Physics-Mathematics School]]. Burago received his doctorate in 1994 at [[Saint Petersburg State University]] under the supervision of [[Anatoly Vershik]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=58657}}</ref> He was at the [[Steklov Institute]] in Saint Petersburg and is now a professor at [[Pennsylvania State University]]'s Center for Dynamical Systems and Geometry.

In 1992, he was awarded the prize of the [[Saint Petersburg Mathematical Society]]. In 1998, he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Burago, Dmitri|year=1998|chapter=Hard balls gas and Alexandrov spaces of curvature bounded above|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians: Berlin, 1998, August 18–27|volume=2|pages=289–298|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011706000}}</ref> In 2014, he was awarded the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] with Yuri Burago and [[Sergei Ivanov (mathematician)|Sergei Vladimirovich Ivanov]] for their book ''A course in metric geometry''.<ref>{{cite web|title= A Course in Metric Geometry book wins prize for mathematical exposition|date=16 January 2014|website=Penn State News|url=https://news.psu.edu/story/300529/2014/01/16/academics/course-metric-geometry-book-wins-prize-mathematical-exposition}}</ref>
